# Architecture

## The RSSM in one paragraph

`rssmlite` implements a **Recurrent State-Space Model (RSSM)**, the world-model
backbone introduced by Hafner et al. in DreamerV1/V2 and refined in DreamerV3
(2023). The model learns a compact latent representation of an environment's
dynamics entirely from the agent's own experience — no external data, no
hand-engineered reward shaping — so that a policy can be trained entirely in
*imagination* (imagined rollouts generated by the learned model) rather than by
collecting expensive real environment transitions.

---

## State representation

At every timestep `t`, the world model maintains a two-part state:

```
deter_t  ∈  R^{deter_dim}          deterministic, recurrent (h_t from GRU)
stoch_t  ∈  {0,1}^{C × K}          stochastic, categorical (C groups, K classes each)
feature_t = concat(deter_t, flatten(stoch_t))   — what every head reads
```

**Why two parts?**

- The deterministic part (`deter`) provides a smooth, gradient-friendly
  memory of history. Because it's the GRU's hidden state it can in principle
  remember arbitrarily far back (in practice limited by vanishing gradients,
  but good enough for the target environments).
- The stochastic part (`stoch`) provides representational capacity that can
  capture multimodal futures. A deterministic-only model can only predict one
  future; the stochastic latent lets the model hedge. The categorical
  parameterization (C × K one-hot groups) is preferred over a diagonal
  Gaussian because it produces sharper representations and avoids the
  posterior collapse problem that Gaussian VAEs suffer from (Hafner et al.
  2023, §2).

---

## Forward pass

```
Observe (training, has real observation):

  embed_t   = Encoder(symlog(obs_t))
  deter_t   = GRUCell(pre_gru(concat(stoch_{t-1}, action_{t-1})), deter_{t-1})
  prior_t   = PriorNet(deter_t)            # prior: no observation
  post_t    = PosteriorNet(deter_t, embed_t)  # posterior: uses real obs
  stoch_t   ~ StraightThrough(post_t)      # discrete sample, gradient flows

Imagine (inference, no observation):

  deter_t   = GRUCell(pre_gru(concat(stoch_{t-1}, action_{t-1})), deter_{t-1})
  stoch_t   ~ StraightThrough(PriorNet(deter_t))   # prior only
```

---

## Training objective

The world model is trained to minimise four terms simultaneously:

| Term | What it trains | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Reconstruction loss | Decoder to predict symlog(obs) from feature | MSE in symlog space |
| Reward loss | RewardHead to predict symlog(reward) | MSE in symlog space |
| Continue loss | ContinueHead to predict P(not done) | BCE |
| KL loss | Posterior close to prior; prior tracks posterior | KL balancing + free bits |

**symlog scaling** (Hafner et al. 2023, §A): `symlog(x) = sign(x) * log(1 + |x|)`.
Applied to observations and rewards before they enter the network, and to
predictions before computing reconstruction loss. This makes the loss
insensitive to the absolute scale of different environments (CartPole
observations are O(1); LunarLander velocities can be O(10)) without needing
per-environment normalisation.

**KL balancing** (α=0.8): instead of minimising `KL(posterior || prior)` alone
(which incentivises the model to move the prior toward the posterior rather than
learn a useful one), we minimise a weighted sum:

```
α · KL(sg(post) || prior) + (1-α) · KL(post || sg(prior))
```

The first term (weight α=0.8) trains the prior aggressively. The second
(weight 0.2) keeps the posterior honest. `sg` = stop-gradient.

**Free bits** (1.0 nats per group): the KL is clamped from below at
`free_bits`, so the model gets that much representational budget "for free"
without penalty. Prevents posterior collapse without requiring careful
β-annealing schedules.

---

## Actor-critic (imagination)

```
for t = 1..H:
    action_t, entropy_t = Actor(feature_t)
    deter_{t+1}, stoch_{t+1} = RSSM.imagine_step(deter_t, stoch_t, action_t)

reward_t = symexp(RewardHead(feature_t))
continue_t = sigmoid(ContinueHead(feature_t))
value_t = Critic(feature_t)

returns_t = lambda_return(reward, continue, value, γ=0.99, λ=0.95)

actor_loss  = -mean(returns) - entropy_coef * mean(entropy)
critic_loss = MSE(Critic(feature), returns.detach())
```

The actor loss backpropagates straight through the imagined rollout (no
REINFORCE/score-function estimator) because actions are differentiable
straight-through categorical samples.

---

## Swappable backbone

`RSSM` accepts any `dynamics` object that implements:

```python
dynamics.forward(deter, stoch, action) -> deter   # one recurrent step
dynamics.prior_logits(deter) -> logits             # (B, C, K) prior
```

`GRUDynamics` is the default. `TransformerDynamics` (roadmap P2, ablation
study) will implement the same interface, so `RSSM` never changes.

---

## File map

```
src/rssmlite/
  utils.py          symlog, symexp, KL balancing, mlp(), straight-through sample
  backbones/gru.py  GRUDynamics — the default swappable backbone
  networks.py       Encoder, PosteriorNet, Decoder, RewardHead, ContinueHead
  rssm.py           RSSM — composes the above; observe() and imagine()
  actor_critic.py   Actor, Critic, lambda_return()
  agent.py          RSSMAgent — orchestrates training, checkpointing, eval
  replay_buffer.py  ReplayBuffer — episode storage and fixed-length sampling
  env_utils.py      collect_episode(), encode_action(), action_dim_of()
  evaluation.py     reconstruction_report(), plot_reconstruction(), compare_sample_efficiency()
```
